record.paper_title: Selected Open Problems in Discrete Geometry and Optimization
record.original_question: In spherical space S^d and hyperbolic space H^d, for a fixed ball and a variable simplex of prescribed volume V, is the volume of the intersection of the ball and the simplex maximized when the simplex is regular and concentric with the ball?

evidence.quote: The maximum volume of the intersection of a fixed ball in Ed and a variable simplex of given volume V is attained when the simplex is regular and concentric with the ball. Question 6. Show that the above statement holds true in spherical and hyperbolic space as well.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M^d$ denote either the $d$-dimensional spherical space $S^d$ (with $d \geq 2$) or the $d$-dimensional hyperbolic space $H^d$, each endowed with its standard Riemannian metric of constant sectional curvature $+1$ or $-1$ respectively. By a ball in $M^d$ we mean a geodesic ball, and by a simplex we mean the geodesically convex hull of $d+1$ points in general position. A simplex is called regular if its isometry group acts transitively on its vertices, and it is called concentric with a given ball if the center of the ball coincides with the centroid (equivalently, the circumcenter) of the simplex.

Fix a geodesic ball $B \subset M^d$ and a positive real number $V$ (taken less than the total volume of $M^d$ in the spherical case). Among all simplices $S \subset M^d$ of volume exactly $V$, prove or disprove the following statement: the volume of the intersection $B \cap S$ is maximized precisely when $S$ is regular and concentric with $B$.
artifact.category_tag: Discrete geometry in spaces of constant curvature
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not locate a published resolution of the spherical and hyperbolic analogues of the ball–simplex intersection maximization problem. Related results in the area (such as the fact that the maximum-volume simplex contained in a hyperbolic ball is regular, and analogous packing-density results of Böröczky) are known, but no source verifies the precise statement that the volume of the intersection of a fixed ball with a simplex of prescribed volume in $S^d$ or $H^d$ is maximized by the regular concentric simplex. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Simplices of Maximal Volume or Minimal Total Edge Length in Hyperbolic Space
status_evidence.snippet: Amongst all simplices in a closed geodesic ball, the simplex of maximal volume is regular.
status_evidence.claim: Related extremal result establishing regularity of maximizers, but not addressing the intersection volume problem.

status_evidence.title: Volumes of Regular Hyperbolic Simplices
status_evidence.snippet: Explicit formulas for volumes of regular simplices in spherical/hyperbolic geometry.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on regular simplex volumes in constant curvature spaces, with no resolution of the intersection problem cited.
